content.comment_body: Hello, I would like the website I created with [product_name] Web Editor to be accessible and functional both locally on the PLC and externally via PC or mobile using a URL. After publishing the website to the PLC, it works with physical switches, and their responses are visible on the web page, but the site doesn't respond to mouse clicks—after clicking a button, the loading symbol appears and then nothing happens. Additionally, if I don't download the website to the PLC, it works from a PC or mobile, but I wish to achieve both results. Can someone point out what I might be doing incorrectly or how to resolve this? Also, inputs labeled 'I' are not clickable on the web page through [product_name] Web Editor. For reference, I am using [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] Web Editor [version_no].
Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Please note that this is an English-speaking forum; kindly post your future messages in English. Thank you.
Have you seen this topic: AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess is no longer available?
Inputs of the 'I' type—digital inputs—cannot be switched remotely via [product_name] Web Editor or through cloud solutions. You can only display the status of these inputs.

Sorry, AWS has changed its authorization policy guidelines, which is why the 'AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess' permission is no longer available. You may add authorization (policy) in IAM under Permissions for the user: '[BINARY_DATA_REMOVED]'. Consequently, transfer of [product_name] Web Editor websites to AWS is now possible again. Due to this change, Elastic Beanstalk no longer works on both PLC and remote devices simultaneously—only externally via a designated URL. I edited the settings using attachments but the original issue remains. Apologies if I misunderstood; it's my first experience with AWS so I am still learning.

Hello, The built-in Web Server of [product_name] [version_no] and the cloud connection cannot operate simultaneously. Also, it is not possible to control inputs (DI and AI) of [product_name] hardware from external devices; these inputs can only be read, not modified. If you upload your [product_name] Web Editor project to AWS Cloud, you can use its dashboard over the Internet. The local Web Server is only accessible when directly connected. Using AWS offers more flexibility and supports access from multiple devices. Hope this clarifies things.

Sorry, AWS recently updated its authorization policies, which is why the 'AWSElasticBeanstalkFullAccess' policy is unavailable. You can add the necessary authorization in IAM under Permissions for the user: '[BINARY_DATA_REMOVED]'. With this, [product_name] Web Editor site transfers to AWS are working again. So, following this modification, Elastic Beanstalk is now operational only externally via a specific URL, not both locally and externally. After changing settings with the provided attachments, the initial issue remains. This is my first time using AWS, so I'm still adapting. Then I received a reply from [user_name].

Thank you all for your responses—my apologies for any confusion, as this is my first time posting in the forum. I hope my explanation is clear; I used Google Translate and am unsure if the translation is perfect.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are encountering limitations when using a web page created with [product_name] Web Editor on [product_name] [version_no], particularly regarding dual operation both locally on the PLC and remotely via AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The web page can interact with physical switches locally, but web-based controls do not function as expected. When accessed only remotely, the page works but lacks simultaneous local control. There are also uncertainties about the interactive capabilities of digital inputs ('I') and recent AWS policy changes impacting platform access.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the web page created with [product_name] Web Editor to provide seamless monitoring and control of their PLC system from both local and remote devices, with identical interactivity for switches and inputs from either access point.
gain_keywords: simultaneous local and remote web access
monitoring and control from any device
